subject: Concurrency & rate limits — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency & rate limits — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and action items so we have alignment before we dig into formal quota proposals: 

Key SLOs and constraints you mentioned:
- Latency: P95 <= 100ms for short completions (<= 128 tokens). For longer completions we agreed on P95 <= 300ms.
- Streaming: chat endpoint must stream progressively (first-token < 50ms ideal) and support chunked delivery for real-time UI.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline steady-state ~80 qps, peak concurrency up to ~500 simultaneous parallel requests during marketing promos.
- Connection model: you prefer connection pooling with keep-alive; potentially HTTP/2 or WebSocket for streaming sessions.
- Per-tenant limits: we need per-user/tenant throttles plus a global account quota to protect against noisy actors.

What we need from you to finalize a proposal:
1) Confirm the 500 concurrent peak number (is that simultaneous open requests or concurrent active tokens-in-flight?).
2) Share a 24h sample of traffic shape (peak 5-min, avg qps, token distribution) — a CSV is fine.
3) Indicate whether you plan to use long-lived WebSocket sessions or short-lived HTTP requests with chunked streaming.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We'll draft 2 quota options: (A) Reserved concurrency (Dedicated) with burst envelope, (B) Hosted quota with dynamic burst and token-based billing.
- Laura will sketch the rate-limit/quotas proposal (attached) and include recommended TCP/streaming settings.
- If needed, we can run a small pilot to validate latency under your peak patterns.

I'm attaching the SLO worksheet and our initial proposal draft. Laura/Dylan — adding you both to own the rate-limit design and SRE questions.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: acme-slo-table.xlsx, redwood-rate-limits-proposal.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.io>

Subject: Re: Concurrency & rate limits — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A few clarifications from SRE/engineering side (copied the SRE alias for visibility):

- Concurrency definition: when I said ~500 concurrent requests I meant "concurrent active requests" (requests with tokens in-flight). During promo peaks we see ~500–650 active requests for ~10–15 minute windows. Baseline steady state is closer to 60–90 qps.
- Streaming behavior: chat will use long-lived sessions for many users (WebSocket preferred). For the classic REST path we'll do HTTP/2 with chunked responses for fallback. We care a lot about first-token latency for perceived responsiveness.
- Connection limits: our load balancer creates many short-lived connections; we prefer a connection pooling behavior on the client to reduce TCP churn. What's Redwood's recommendation on max concurrent streams per connection and per-IP connection caps?

Attached a sanitized traffic sample (acme-sre-traffic.csv) that shows token distribution and 5-min peaks. We can provide more if needed.

Also, procurement will need a proposed committed concurrency number and burst policy to size the contract. If Redwood can propose a committed baseline + burst envelope that maps to cost, that will speed procurement.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Engineering — Acme Analytics
alex.johnson@acme.io | +1 212-555-0199

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency & rate limits — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — thanks for the sample and the clarifications. Based on the traffic CSV and the SLO targets, here are two pragmatic options we recommend (summary first, details below):

Option A — Dedicated reserved concurrency (recommended for tight SLOs):
- Committed baseline concurrency: 200 concurrent active requests (guaranteed).
- Burst envelope: allow bursts up to 600 concurrent active requests for up to 15 minutes per hour (automated shaping).
- Streaming: use our Dedicated streaming tier with WebSocket support and prioritized scheduling to meet first-token <50ms for chat.
- Pricing: monthly reserved capacity + overage on consumed tokens above baseline.

Option B — Hosted quota with dynamic burst (lower commitment):
- Soft quota: 100 baseline concurrency throttled at 95% of baseline; burst up to 400 for short windows with best-effort warm scaling.
- Token-based billing with per-minute smoothing to avoid token spikes billing surprises.
- Streaming: supported via HTTP/2 chunked streaming; WebSocket available as an add-on.

Connection/streaming recommendations:
- For HTTP/2: aim for ~100 concurrent streams per connection; recommend client-side connection pooling with keep-alive to reuse TLS sessions and lower CPU/TCP resource usage.
- For WebSocket: long-lived sessions are fine; we'll set per-connection write windows and per-tenant socket limits to prevent noisy neighbors.
- Per-IP connection caps: we usually enforce conservative per-IP caps (configurable) to defend against accidental DDoS patterns — we'll provide suggested settings after you share whether you have many NATed IPs behind a small set of egress addresses.

Pilot and measurement plan:
1) Share a 24–72h traffic sample (you already sent one — thank you).
2) Redwood runs a small-scale pilot with your peak-shaped replay to validate tail latency and streaming first-token.
3) If pilot results meet SLOs, we finalize the committed baseline and burst envelope in the commercial proposal.

I've attached the detailed rate-limits proposal and an SLO workbook with the math mapping concurrency -> token/sec -> cost. Marissa/dylan — next steps for internal engineering: Dylan, can you confirm the technical changes needed for HTTP/2 connection pool guidance and provide an estimate on engineering effort for the WebSocket integration if Acme chooses that path?

Proposed follow-up: Thu Aug 13 at 10:00am PT for a 30m alignment call to confirm baseline/burst and procurement asks.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
